answer: Each established agent may sponsor at most two newcomers and must lock a jade-denominated bond equal to thirty days of average mining rewards for each of them. A public graph mirror records those sponsorship edges. If later clustering shows the newcomers share funding paths or near-identical work traces with the sponsor or each other, that bond is slashed and the umber admission marks on those accounts are revoked. Because a clone swarm consumes scarce sponsorship slots and burns real capital, mass identity farming becomes expensive.
